content_groups.group_title: Q1. What is the purpose of the anomaly scan?

blocks.text: To assess fetal anatomy systematically and identify structural abnormalities, while also assessing fetal growth, placenta and amniotic fluid.

content_groups.group_title: Q2. Does a normal anomaly scan guarantee a normal baby?

blocks.text: No. Ultrasound cannot detect every structural, genetic or developmental abnormality.

content_groups.group_title: Q3. What views are important in assessing the fetal brain?

blocks.text: Ventricles, midline structures, cavum septum pellucidum, cerebellum and posterior fossa, among others.

content_groups.group_title: Q4. What cardiac views are important?

blocks.text: Four-chamber view and assessment of the ventricular outflow tracts, with additional views when indicated.

content_groups.group_title: Q5. What is the difference between omphalocele and gastroschisis?

blocks.text: Omphalocele is usually a midline/umbilical defect covered by a membrane and has stronger associations with chromosomal abnormalities. Gastroschisis is usually paraumbilical, with exposed bowel and no covering membrane.
Ruptured membranes, placental insufficiency and fetal renal/urinary abnormalities are important causes.
Maternal diabetes, multiple pregnancy, fetal swallowing/structural abnormalities and idiopathic causes.

content_groups.group_title: Q8. What is a single umbilical artery?

blocks.text: An umbilical cord with one artery and one vein instead of the normal two arteries and one vein.

content_groups.group_title: Q9. What would you do if the anomaly scan is incomplete?

blocks.text: Arrange repeat imaging to obtain the required views rather than falsely reporting the anatomy as normal.

content_groups.group_title: Q10. What should you do when an abnormality is identified?

blocks.text: Confirm and characterize the finding, arrange appropriate specialist/fetal medicine assessment, consider relevant genetic or other investigations and provide non-directive counselling and support.

blocks.text: The examiner is assessing your communication skills, not just your ultrasound knowledge.
If shown a normal anomaly scan, you can say:

"This is a singleton intrauterine pregnancy with fetal biometry appropriate for the established gestational age. The fetal head and intracranial structures visualised appear normal. The facial profile and upper lip appear normal. The spine is intact on the views obtained. The four-chamber cardiac view and outflow tracts appear satisfactory. The chest, diaphragm and abdominal organs visualised appear normal. Both kidneys and the bladder are identified. The abdominal wall and umbilical cord insertion appear normal, and a three-vessel cord is identified. The limbs visualised appear normal. The placenta is appropriately located and clear of the internal cervical os. Amniotic fluid volume appears normal. No obvious major structural abnormality is identified on this examination."
"I would correlate these findings with the clinical history, previous screening results and the formal ultrasound report."
